n: Business Email Compromise and Invoice Redirection
ds: Criminals compromise or spoof email accounts to impersonate executives or suppliers and redirect payments to accounts they control. Typical outcomes are urgent wire requests or changed bank details on genuine invoices.

src.t: FinCEN, Updated Advisory on Email Compromise Fraud Schemes Targeting Vulnerable Business Processes, FIN-2019-A005 (2019)
FBI IC3, Business E-Mail Compromise: The $55 Billion Scam (PSA I-091124-PSA, 2024)
UK Finance, Annual Fraud Report (specify year, e.g. 2025)

cn.rt: Consumers pay deposits or settlement funds to redirected details on spoofed invoices (e.g. conveyancing, tradespeople); business wire variants are out of scope.

rat: Business payment redirection via email compromise, mostly wires.

ind.n: Change of beneficiary bank details close to a payment
ind.cx: Victim-side: supplier payment details are altered shortly before an invoice is due, via email or portal.
ind.ds: Victim-side: supplier payment details are altered shortly before an invoice is due, via email or portal.

ind.n: Urgent confidential payment request from a senior executive
ind.cx: Victim-side: finance staff receive a request, often outside normal workflow, to wire funds quickly and not discuss it.
ind.ds: Staff receive urgent, confidential requests, or changes to beneficiary details, directing payment to a new beneficiary outside normal workflow.
ind.cn: Urgent payment instruction or payment-detail change outside normal process

ind.n: Lookalike or recently registered sender domain
ind.cx: Spoofed email domain or reply-to differs subtly from the genuine counterparty.
ind.ds: Spoofed email domain or reply-to differs subtly from the genuine counterparty.

ind.n: First payment to a new beneficiary in a different jurisdiction
ind.cx: Victim-side: payment to a new account, often foreign, unrelated to the supplier's usual country.
ind.ds: Victim-side: payment to a new account, often foreign, unrelated to the supplier's usual country.

ind.n: Business account receives funds then moves them offshore or to crypto quickly
ind.cx: Mule-side: a recipient account (often newly opened or a shell) forwards BEC proceeds within hours.
ind.ds: Incoming funds are quickly sent abroad or converted to virtual assets soon after being credited.
ind.cn: Rapid movement offshore or to crypto after receipt

ind.n: Invoice amount or format differs from prior invoices
ind.cx: Victim-side: genuine-looking invoice has altered layout, round figures or inconsistent references.
ind.ds: Victim-side: genuine-looking invoice has altered layout, round figures or inconsistent references.

ind.n: Payment initiated outside normal approval chain
ind.cx: Victim-side: bypass of the usual purchase order or approval, or approver working remotely at odd hours.
ind.ds: bypass of the usual purchase order or approval, or approver working remotely at odd hours.

ind.n: Shell or newly formed company receiving corporate payments
ind.cx: Mule-side: beneficiary has little trading footprint, a virtual office or recent incorporation.
ind.ds: Entity has no staff, premises, website or trading history consistent with its stated activity, yet receives significant payments.
ind.cn: Shell entity with no operating footprint

ind.n: Corporate login from unusual location or after mailbox rule change
ind.cx: Compromise indicator: mailbox forwarding rules and unfamiliar logins precede payment fraud.
ind.ds: mailbox forwarding rules and unfamiliar logins precede payment fraud.

ctl.ds: Verifies instructions, detail changes and unusual requests by contacting the customer on a channel held on file, never one supplied in the request. It defeats impersonation and account takeover.

Checks the payee name against the destination account before release and warns on no-match or close-match, and flags payee-name mismatches against contracted entities. It interrupts misdirected, spoofed and fraudulent payments.

ctl.n: Vendor master-data and bank-detail change control
ctl.ds: Requires independent verification and review of any new or changed supplier bank details before the next payment run, including challenge of redirections to third-country accounts. It stops payment-diversion and business-email-compromise fraud.

Trains branch, contact-centre and relationship staff to ask open questions, recognise coaching, coercion, pressure and evasion and escalate with authority to pause. It strengthens the human control at the point of contact.

ctl.n: Segregation of duties and dual authorisation
ctl.ds: Ensures no single person can create, approve and release a payment or master-data change, requiring an independent second approver. It controls insider and impersonation fraud.
Monitors for spoofed domains, fake apps, adverts, numbers and fraudulent campaigns, and arranges takedown, suspension and customer alerts. It removes criminal infrastructure.
Analyses typing, navigation, remote-access tooling, call-in-progress signals and deviation from baseline to spot coached, scripted or hijacked sessions. It detects coercion and takeover.

Matches accounts, devices, identifiers and beneficiaries against industry fraud sharing and ingests law-enforcement, commercial and open-source threat feeds, including victim reports from other institutions. It catches known bad actors early.

ctl.n: Funds hold, freeze and recall procedure
ctl.ds: Provides a defined, legally grounded capability to restrict, hold, freeze or recall funds and accounts pending review or on confirmed exposure, with clear triggers and approvers. It stops onward dissipation of suspected illicit funds.
Model that scores inbound-then-outbound pass-through, new-payee churn, counterparty diversity and profile mismatch to flag likely mule accounts. It prioritises accounts for review and restriction.

Checks identity and supporting documents for tampering, forgery, template reuse and internal inconsistency, and corroborates their data against authoritative or reliable independent sources. It exposes altered or counterfeit credentials that pass a visual check.
Tracks cases, outcomes, losses and false positives, routes concerns across fraud, sanctions and anti-corruption teams and feeds outcomes into tuning and appetite. It supports consistent handling.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

Remote verification of a person's identity using document capture, biometric matching and liveness or anti-spoofing checks, or a trusted digital identity. It reduces impersonation, synthetic identities and account opening with stolen or fabricated credentials.
Requires phishing-resistant authentication and additional verification on risky sessions, credential or payee changes and large payments. It blocks unauthorised access and payments.
